title: Power Apps: Power Apps CLI commands to find connectors and create connections for code apps
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap facts, connector commands, licensing alternatives and governance controls are supported. The cited pages opened successfully, and targeted searches did not establish the CLI-specific controls or charges that the briefing reports as undocumented.

claims.claim: The roadmap change adds CLI commands for developers to discover available connectors.
claims.quote: The Power Apps CLI adds new commands that let developers discover available connectors and create connections directly from the command line.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Developers can create connections and wire connectors into code apps without switching tools or configuring connections in the maker portal.
claims.quote: This enables developers to wire connectors into code apps as part of their normal development workflow, without switching tools or manually configuring connections in the maker portal.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: After rollout; Open questions
claims.claim: The roadmap describes new code app agent.md files and how-to documentation for coding-agent connector discovery and connection creation.
claims.quote: New code app agent.md files and code app how-to documentation show how coding agents can handle connector discovery and connection creation as part of end-to-end prompt-to-app workflows.

claims.claim: Enable code apps is at Power Platform admin center > Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Product > Features > Power Apps code apps > Enable code apps.
claims.quote: Go to Manage > Environments > select the environment where you use code apps. Go to Settings > Expand the Product subsection > Select Features. Go to the feature Power Apps code apps and use the Enable code apps toggle to turn it on.

claims.claim: No documented runnable automation operation sets the code apps environment toggle.
claims.quote: Searched: PowerAppsAllowCodeApps; PowerApps_AllowCodeApps; code apps enable pac admin API; update environment settings API Set-AdminPowerAppEnvironment. Read SDK property, pac admin results and Environment Management Settings PATCH reference; no request property is documented for this setting.

claims.claim: Environment groups and rules can configure the code apps setting for multiple environments at once.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Why it matters; rationale: impact
claims.claim: The Enable code apps environment setting defaults to Off.
claims.quote: | Setting | Description | Default value | ... | Enable code apps | Allow users to bring apps they created outside of Power Apps and run them in Power Apps. If this setting is turned off, those apps don't run. ... | Off |

claims.claim: Code apps do not run when the Enable code apps setting is turned off.
claims.quote: Allow users to bring apps they created outside of Power Apps and run them in Power Apps. If this setting is turned off, those apps don't run.

claims.claim: The new connector commands are a maker-chosen capability, recorded as user-opt-in, within environments enabled for code apps.
claims.quote: Use the Power Apps CLI to find connectors and create a connection without leaving your terminal or opening Power Apps. ... Use pa connection create to create a connection in the environment configured for the code app:

claims.where: summary; Why it matters; Governance controls
claims.claim: Microsoft documents no separate admin switch or new admin action specific to these connector commands.
claims.quote: Searched: "code apps" "CLI" admin disable connector commands; "code apps" enable pac admin API. Opened code apps overview, create-connection, CLI reference, npm-quickstart and feature settings; found the existing environment toggle, not a command-specific switch or rollout action.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Governance guidance

claims.quote: Use the connection ID when you add the connector as a data source to the code app.

claims.claim: A blockable connector in an existing policy is blocked at Power Platform admin center > Security > Settings > Data and privacy > Data policy > policy > Edit Policy > Prebuilt connectors > connector > Block.
claims.quote: Select Security ... under Settings, select Data and privacy ... select the Data policy section. ... select a policy, and then select Edit Policy. ... Select the Prebuilt connectors step ... For connectors like SharePoint that aren't blockable, the Block action isn't available

claims.claim: Add-ConnectorsToPolicy -PolicyName <policy-guid> -Connectors <connector-objects> -Classification <General|Confidential|Blocked> changes the connectors' group in the specified DLP policy.
claims.quote: Add-ConnectorsToPolicy [-PolicyName] <String> [-Classification] <String> [-Connectors] <Object[]> ... If any of the connectors are already classified in a different group, they are moved to the specified group. ... The policy name (GUID).

claims.claim: The Classification values General, Confidential and Blocked mean Non-business, Business and Blocked respectively.
claims.quote: Allowed values are 'General', 'Confidential', and 'Blocked' (for Non-business, Business, and Blocked, respectively).

claims.claim: Each object passed through Connectors requires id, type and name properties.
claims.quote: Each entry in the list is required to have 3 properties: id: The unique identifier of the connector. ... type: The type of the connector: ... name: The friendly name of the connector

claims.where: controls[1].governs; controls[1].scope; Governance controls; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Data policies govern connector use and combinations within the environments in their scope.
claims.quote: Business: Connectors for sensitive data. Connectors in this group can't share data with connectors in other groups. ... Blocked: Blocked connectors can't be used where this policy is applied.

claims.claim: The tenant-level data policy instructions require the Power Platform Administrator role.
claims.quote: To follow the steps described in this article for tenant-level policies, sign in as a user with the Power Platform Administrator role.

claims.claim: Environment-level data policy instructions require Power Apps Environment Admin permissions, subject to the Dataverse exception.
claims.quote: To follow the steps for environment-level policies, you need to have Power Apps Environment Admin permissions.

claims.claim: For environments with a Dataverse database, the data policy instructions require the System Administrator role instead.
claims.quote: For environments with a Dataverse database, you need to be assigned the System Administrator role instead.

claims.claim: Learn does not distinguish which of these CLI commands are in preview and which are generally available.
claims.quote: Searched: "code apps" "connection create" preview. Read CLI, create-connection, connect-to-data and npm-quickstart. The Copilot quickstart names a preview plugin and pac code is preview; neither assigns a phase to pa connector list or pa connection create.
